newsitem.title: USA: Chinese, Hong Kong ADRs unmoved by Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Chinese, Hong Kong ADRs unmoved by Deng's death.

text.p: The death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping left New York markets in Chinese and Hong Kong American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) unmoved on Wednesday, traders said.
"There hasn't been any kind of follow-through on Chinese and Hong Kong ADRs," a trader said. "I don't seen any major panic in New York."
China's official news agency reported Deng, 93, died late on Wednesday of complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection.
Among leading ADRs, Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Ltd was unchanged at 4-1/2, and Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd was off 3/8 to 17 in light trade.
Jardine Fleming China Region Fund Inc was unchanged at 11-5/8 and Shandong Huaneng Power Development Co Ltd dropped 1/8 to 10-3/8.
Traders said markets had long factored in Deng's death.
"Any far-thinking trader has already figured, 'Hey, he's 93, he's not going to live another 10 years'," a dealer said.
Deng's death also is seen leading to bargain-hunting as investors fearful of potential upheaval unload Chinese and Hong Kong shares.
"Change creates uncertainty, uncertainty creates nervousness, nervousness creates sellers," a trader said.
